title: TB4 KVM v1 owner decision catalog

decisions.title: 1. Start-up selection
decisions.question: When both hosts are attached at power-up, what should happen?
decisions.rationale: Default: restore the last safe host; otherwise select HOST A. It avoids a surprise desk change after a power event.
decisions.boundary: This still waits for supported Type-C/PD discovery. It cannot energise both hosts.

options.label: Restore the last safe host; otherwise HOST A

decisions.title: 2. Selected-host charging
decisions.question: What charging promise should v1 make to the selected host?
decisions.rationale: Default: up to 60 W for the selected host, with no promised charging for the unselected host.
decisions.boundary: The supply budget, dock power ownership and reverse-current protection still need reference-backed proof.

options.label: Up to 60 W selected host; none promised to the other

decisions.title: 3. Active-host removal
decisions.question: When the selected host disconnects, should the dock move automatically?
decisions.rationale: Default: show the loss and wait for a button press. It avoids an unexpected desktop change.
decisions.boundary: Automatic failover needs a reference-supported discovery and guard sequence before it can be promised.

options.label: Auto-fail over only after a validated guard sequence

decisions.title: 4. Downstream compatibility
decisions.question: What should v1 promise downstream?
decisions.rationale: Default: validate the named OWC Thunderbolt Dock 96W first, rather than claiming arbitrary-dock support.
decisions.boundary: The named dock still needs recorded cable, display, firmware and functional validation evidence.

options.label: Broader devices only after separate validation

decisions.title: 5. External-power loss
decisions.question: What should the KVM do if its external supply is absent or fails?
decisions.rationale: Default: isolate both hosts and do not promise dock-powered pass-through.
decisions.boundary: The detailed VBUS, VCONN and discharge policy must come from the accepted reference design.

options.label: Isolate both hosts; no pass-through promise

decisions.title: 6. Switching experience
decisions.question: What should the v1 validation plan target for switching?
decisions.rationale: Default: record each switching stage first; do not promise a time until the supported path is measured.
decisions.boundary: The owner can set a desired experience, but vendor/reference timing and safety checks control the actual sequence.

options.label: Record before making a time promise
Aim for under 10 seconds, subject to validation

decisions.title: 7. Status surface
decisions.question: What should the indicator or optional display communicate?
decisions.rationale: Default: selected host plus switching, waiting and fault state. Add PD/link facts only when the controller supports them.
decisions.boundary: It must not imply live throughput, compliance or host activity without named evidence.

options.label: Selected host and truthful state only

decisions.title: 8. Mechanical envelope
decisions.question: What physical-size boundary should define a successful v1?
decisions.rationale: Default: keep the three-port main unit, onboard control and protected remote-pod connector minimal, but defer a hard size promise until the released PCB and thermal map are measured.
decisions.boundary: A compact intention is not a dimension. Choose a maximum below only as an owner target; PCB clearances, cable bend space, insulation and cooling can require a reviewed change.

options.label: Defer exact size until PCB and thermal measurements
Target at most 180 × 120 × 45 mm, excluding power brick and cables
